changelog: [Core Principles]: Strengthened the final 'when in doubt, split' bullet into an explicit left-to-right scanning rule: once a connective-ending or punctuation boundary is reached and it already closes a complete predicate, take that split immediately rather than waiting for a later, 'safer-looking' boundary further on. This directly targets under-segmentation (long multi-clause sentences left whole despite clear early connective/punctuation boundaries) without adding any new prohibition — it only clarifies the existing bias-to-split principle.

[Examples — Segment]: Added three new generalized examples demonstrating the three most common missed-split patterns from measurement: (a) splitting immediately after a complete clause followed by 그런데/근데, (b) splitting at a mid-utterance '?' before further speech continues, (c) splitting a '-고' coordination where each side has its own distinct subject and verb. No examples were removed since the section remains under the 12-example cap (11/12).
